comparator.name: Pharmaceutical Sciences (Farmaceutische Wetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER lists the compulsory components and exact credits: 60 EC in Year 1, 60 EC in Year 2, and in Year 3 two 6-EC major courses, an 18-EC Bachelorproject FAR and 30 EC of open profiling space. Zero-credit lab safety, language test and tutorials are omitted from credit-bearing components but remain requirements. The OER places Project moderne ontwikkelingen in de farmaceutische wetenschappen in Year 1, whereas the general curriculum webpage places it under Year 2; this reconstruction follows the formal OER placement. No formal graduation specializations exist under OER Article 10.2; chemistry- and biology-focused minors are optional uses of the open space. Teaching language is Dutch.

exception.reason: VU’s compulsory core centers on medicinal and organic chemistry, molecule design and synthesis, pharmacokinetics, bioanalysis, molecular pharmacology and toxicology laboratory work, followed by an 18-EC pharmaceutical research project. UCR offers relevant biology, biochemistry, pharmacology and disease courses, but no organic chemistry or synthesis sequence, pharmaceutical chemistry laboratory, ADME course, molecular toxicology practical or drug-design capstone. A 24-course biomedical path would represent a different field and obscure the chemical drug-discovery core of this target. The optional biology- or chemistry-focused minor does not remove that compulsory gap.
exception.curriculumContext: The adopted 2026–27 OER specifies a 180-EC compulsory major plus 30 EC of genuinely open first-semester third-year profiling space. Its formal Year 1 placement of the modern-developments project takes precedence over the broad prospectus year grouping. Zero-EC safety, tutorial and language-test requirements are acknowledged without inventing credit.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked the 151 UCR course rows in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx for names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned term availability. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics address cellular disease and some pharmacological context. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry is environmental chemistry, not medicinal synthesis. No UCR course teaches the requisite organic synthesis, compound identification and optimization, pharmacokinetics/ADME or toxicological drug-testing practicals as a sustained programme. Those biomedical complements cannot form a defensible closest 24-course Pharmaceutical Sciences comparison.
